title: Choosing, powering and organising your workshop

say: Choosing, powering and organising your workshop.
This is the video for module one of Factory and Workshop Setup.
A workshop is simply a space arranged around your production, so work moves smoothly and safely from raw material to finished product.

say: Bigger is not automatically better. A well-arranged 20 square metre room often produces more than a cluttered 40 square metre one, because people walk less and search less.

say: Step three. Draw a line every time you walk somewhere during one batch. In a poor layout the lines tangle like spaghetti.
For example, Chiamaka in Enugu put a fabric shelf beside her cutting table and saved about 360 metres of walking a day.

panel.rule: Judge every room against your written must-solve list.

say: Landlords often ask for a year's rent in advance, so compare options over 12 months: one-time costs plus 12 months of running costs.

card.title: Compare the full year, not one month

say: A room at home costs Chiamaka about 330,000 naira for the year. It is cheap, but family life and work get in each other's way.

card.title: Compare the full year, not one month

say: A shared cluster workshop costs about 560,000 naira. It splits rent, but needs written agreements on schedules and storage.

card.title: Compare the full year, not one month

say: A rented shop unit costs about 1,150,000 naira, with the rent paid upfront.
She chooses the home room now, with a written plan to move to the cluster when she adds a third machine.

say: Copy the watts from each machine's label and add them up. Chiamaka's machines, iron, bulbs, fans and charger come to 2,300 watts.

panel.heading: Work out what your equipment draws
items: List every machine and its watts from the label
Add them up: this is your total load
Current in amps = watts / 230
Add a 25% margin for motors starting
Generator VA = watts / 0.8

say: Mains supply is nominally 230 volts, so divide watts by 230 to get amps. That is 10 amps.

say: Motors draw extra power when they start, so add 25 percent. That gives 2,875 watts.

say: Usable watts are about 0.8 times a generator's kVA, so she needs roughly a 3.6 kVA set. Or she plans work so the iron and both machines never run together.

panel.rule: Never guess. Check your circuits with an electrician.

say: Give each heavy appliance its own socket, never chain extension boards, and remove any cable with exposed wires or scorch marks.

panel.heading: Electrical and generator safety

cards.d: Heavy appliances get their own socket. Never chain extension boards. Remove cracked or scorched cables.
Ask your electrician for an RCD of no more than 30 mA, and press its test button regularly.
Exhaust has carbon monoxide, which can kill. Cool it before refuelling; store fuel in a closed container.

say: Ask your electrician to fit a residual current device, an RCD, rated at no more than 30 milliamps. Press its test button regularly.

panel.heading: Electrical and generator safety

say: Run generators outdoors only. The exhaust contains carbon monoxide, a gas you cannot see or smell that can kill. Let it cool before refuelling.

say: A workshop does not stay organised by accident. Use 5S. Sort: red-tag anything unsure, and if nobody needs it within a month, it goes.

panel.heading: The 5S cycle
items: Sort: remove what is not needed
Set in order: a fixed home for everything
Shine: clean, and inspect while you clean
Standardise: labels, outlines, photos
Sustain: a daily reset and a weekly score

say: Set in order: a fixed home for everything, near where it is used. A shadow board shows a missing tool at a glance.

say: Some rules protect people and property, so they are never optional. Write them on one page and put it on the wall.
Keep the exit clear. Never leave heat unattended. Keep chemicals labelled, never in drink bottles. Report hazards at once. Switch off and lock up.
Teach these on day one, before the first accident.

panel.heading: Rules that are never optional
items: Exit route and extinguisher never blocked
No machine or heat left on and unattended
Chemicals only in labelled containers
Report spills and hazards immediately
Last person out switches off and locks up

say: To remember. Measure and map first. Compare options over a full year. Work out your amps and add a margin. Keep generators outdoors.
And keep 5S going, with your rules on the wall.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Measure, map and list must-solves first
Compare setup options over 12 months
Watts / 230 = amps; add a margin for motors
Generators run outdoors only
5S is a cycle; rules go on the wall
